rationale: The assistant followed the ideal path: insisted on unplugging, asked for the hand-turn drum check first, correctly read the free-spinning result plus the 'black rubbery strip' as a snapped drive belt, and refused to name an exact belt part without the full model, pointing the customer to the serial plate instead. Calibration was good ('probably snapped' before the visual confirmation) and escalation to an engineer was appropriately conditional. Weaknesses: it never asked about squeaking or advised inspecting the jockey pulley at the same time, gave no warning about sharp edges, and the second reply had a garbled sentence ('It is usually on a sticker...') that relied on the panel to actually ask for the model number.
